children: Markets opened on a cautious note Friday morning, a day after the Nifty 50 suffered its steepest single-session fall since July 8, closing at 23,063.10, down 383.70 points or 1.64 per cent. The Sensex ended the previous session at 73,580.54. Early Friday trade showed marginal recovery, with the Sensex opening at 73,525.92 and quoting at 73,671.44, up 90.90 points or 0.12 per cent, while the Nifty opened at 23,035.00 and was trading at 23,067.45, up just 4.35 points or 0.02 per cent, as of 9.20 am.

The session's top gainers on the Nifty 50 were Bajaj Finserv (₹1,775.10, +0.73 per cent), Shriram Finance (₹996.30, +0.64 per cent), Power Grid (₹268.05, +0.62 per cent), Bajaj Auto (₹11,275.00, +0.60 per cent), and Axis Bank (₹1,193.00, +0.55 per cent). On the losing side, Infosys (₹993.80, -2.04 per cent) and TCS (₹2,047.40, -1.90 per cent) led the decline, followed by ONGC (₹236.02, -1.25 per cent), Wipro (₹161.85, -1.09 per cent), and Tech Mahindra (₹1,530.00, -0.84 per cent).

Thursday's selloff was broad-based, with all major sectoral indices closing in the red. The Financial Services Index was the hardest hit, shedding over 4.35 per cent, weighed down by concerns over the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India's (IRDAI) proposed caps on insurance commissions. IT stocks continued to bleed into Friday's session, with the sector under pressure from rising US bond yields and a stronger dollar.

The global macro backdrop remained hostile. The US 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.22 per cent overnight, a 19-year high, while the 30-year yield climbed to 5.48 per cent, a 22-year high. Brent crude, despite easing slightly, remained elevated above $105 per barrel, following a Houthi missile attack on Saudi Arabia that renewed supply concerns. "High crude and stubborn inflation have increased the probability of another rate hike by the Fed in October," said Dr V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments. "Only a sharp decline in crude prices can help the market rally now."

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) were aggressive sellers on Thursday, offloading equities worth ₹5,027 crore, their largest single-day sell in the month, while domestic institutional investors (DIIs) provided partial support, buying ₹4,301 crore worth of shares. "Domestic buying absorbed most of the outflow but could not prevent the breakdown, indicating that overseas selling remains concentrated enough to pressure index heavyweights," said Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, Founder and CEO of HST Wealth.

On the technical front, analysts flagged 23,000 as the most critical near-term support for the Nifty, backed by heavy put open interest at that level. "As long as the market is trading below 23,300/74,300, weak sentiment is likely to continue," said Shrikant Chouhan, Head of Equity Research at Kotak Securities, adding that a break below 23,000 could drag the index toward 22,800–22,650. Bank Nifty, which closed at 55,438.50 on Thursday, down 1,110 points or 1.96 per cent, faces resistance at 55,700–56,000, with support at 55,000–54,800.

Asian markets traded mixed on Friday, with Japan's Nikkei gaining approximately 1.2 per cent, while Hong Kong was indicated weaker and South Korean markets remained shut for the Chuseok holiday. Wall Street ended nearly flat overnight, with the S&P 500 down 0.02 per cent, the Nasdaq marginally positive, and the Dow Jones declining 0.31 per cent. GIFT Nifty was trading around 23,095–23,115, signalling a flat-to-muted opening for Indian markets.

"Long-term investors can utilise the current weakness in the market to slowly accumulate fundamentally sound stocks, particularly large-caps, now available at attractive valuations," Vijayakumar added. India VIX stood at 12.68, reflecting increased demand for hedging, while the Put-Call Ratio at 0.73 indicated defensive market positioning. A sustained recovery, analysts said, would require the Nifty to reclaim 23,300 and Bank Nifty to return above 56,000.

title: Sensex, Nifty today: Markets open cautiously; IT stocks bleed as crude, yields bite
